title: Evaluation Report on Large Language Models Solving High School Mathematics Questions
extended_summary:
This report evaluates how several large language models (LLMs) perform on high school mathematics examination questions and discusses their potential educational uses. The core question is not whether LLMs improve student learning directly, but how well they can solve high school science/mathematics items across different question types, difficulty levels, and prompting conditions.

The study uses mathematics college entrance examination papers from 2019 to 2023 as the evaluation set. It tests at least eight LLMs, including GLM-4-Flash, ERNIE-Speed-128K, Spark-lite, Hunyuan-lite, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, gemma-2-9b-it, Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, and Yi-34B. The report compares single-solution and multi-solution outputs using accuracy, response time, logical reasoning, guidance sensitivity, and creativity-related metrics. Questions are grouped by type (multiple-choice, fill-in-the-blank, comprehensive) and by difficulty level.

The main findings are that performance varies substantially by model and metric. Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and ERNIE-Speed-128K perform best on accuracy for comprehensive questions and multi-solution tasks, while some models are faster but less accurate. Hunyuan-lite performs well in logical guidance tasks, GLM-4-Flash is strongest in creativity/richness but slow, and gemma-2-9b-it is fastest on some tasks. The report concludes that LLMs show promise as educational tools for mathematics problem-solving, but their reasoning quality, consistency, and efficiency still need improvement before broad instructional use.

identified_tools.name: Qwen
identified_tools.description: Alibaba's Qwen family of large language models for general-purpose text generation, question answering, and reasoning.
identified_tools.use_case: Evaluated as one of eight LLMs on high school mathematics exam questions from 2019-2023, including single-solution and multi-solution prompting, across accuracy, response time, logical reasoning, guidance sensitivity, and creativity.

findings.finding_summary: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct performed strongly on accuracy and efficiency in this mathematics-question evaluation. It had the best single-solution accuracy on fill-in-the-blank questions (0.250, tied) and the best accuracy on intermediate questions (50.00%, tied), and it achieved the top multi-solution accuracy (0.64).
findings.measure: Single-solution accuracy on question types and difficulty levels; multi-solution accuracy

identified_tools.name: LLaMA
identified_tools.description: Meta's LLaMA family of large language models for instruction-following, dialogue, and text generation.
identified_tools.use_case: Evaluated as one of eight LLMs on high school mathematics exam questions from 2019-2023, with outputs assessed for accuracy, response time, logical reasoning, guidance responsiveness, and creativity.

findings.finding_summary: Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct showed relatively balanced but generally middling performance. It had the shortest response times on multiple-choice, fill-in-the-blank, and several difficulty levels, but its accuracy was lower than the best-performing models and its multi-solution accuracy was the lowest at 0.35 (tied).
findings.measure: Response time; single-solution accuracy; multi-solution accuracy

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generic large language model / generative AI chatbot systems used for question answering, reasoning, and text generation without a single named product focus.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper evaluated multiple unnamed LLMs as a class on high school mathematics exam questions, comparing performance on accuracy, timing, logic, guidance, and creativity rather than studying a single product.

findings.finding_summary: Across eight LLMs, performance varied by question type and metric. The strongest single-solution accuracy was on comprehensive questions for ERNIE-Speed-128K (0.950) and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (0.850), while the best multi-solution accuracy was Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (0.64) and ERNIE-Speed-128K (0.63).
findings.measure: Single-solution accuracy, multi-solution accuracy, response time, logic, guidance, creativity

quality_tier_rationale: This is a grey-literature-style evaluation report with unclear methodology, no control group, and no validated causal design. It reports descriptive performance comparisons only, so it does not meet stronger evidence thresholds.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported differences are descriptive and sometimes substantial in raw percentage terms, but there are no effect sizes or causal comparisons to business-as-usual or non-AI supports. The paper therefore suggests potential performance variation rather than demonstrated educational impact.
